mode: Five sequential concept images, with master-frame refinement

assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / portfolio scene.
Create ONE polished landscape image, approximately 1600 x 1000, depicting scene 01 of a five-click UX portfolio narrative. This must look like a premium THREE-DIMENSIONAL architectural illustration with editorial copy, not a flat line drawing, comic, storyboard contact sheet or software screenshot.

The attached blue café neighborhood is the architectural identity and palette reference. Translate it into a restrained, genuinely volumetric 3D miniature: solid white roofs, pale blue faces, cobalt-blue glazing and selected edges, shallow bevels, subtle ambient occlusion and soft white studio lighting. Crisp precise architecture, elegant tiny details, smooth pale-blue capsule/oval tree canopies and carefully proportioned small people. Filled surfaces have volume; avoid wireframe, exaggerated clay blobs or dense outlines. Pure white backdrop and generous negative space. Blue/white only. Editorial sophistication appropriate to a designer with ten years of UX experience. No oversized cartoon protagonist, thought bubbles, frustration squiggles, emoji, oversized pins or gimmicky effects.

COMPOSITION: Match a desktop portfolio frame, 16:10 landscape. Left 39% is uncluttered copy on white, aligned 80px from left. Right 58% is a single continuous 3D corner on a very thin softly edged pale-blue ground tile, fully visible with whitespace around it. The fixed orthographic camera is at a three-quarter isometric angle, around 35° elevation. Typography: an elegant Fraunces-like charcoal editorial serif headline at around 52px, with a clean DM Sans-like supporting text at 20px. Consistent top and bottom margins. Tiny uppercase caption at top-left: "GEOMARKETEER". Small progress label at bottom-left: "01 / 05". No other UI chrome.

ESTABLISH THE MASTER SCENE for subsequent images: foreground-right a distinctive two-storey corner storefront that could become Sid's café, with a white flat roof and inset parapet, two wide upper windows on each visible face, blue-white striped wraparound awnings and a recessed glass ground floor. An unobtrusive cobalt outline identifies the candidate premises; a small neat floating label reads "Potential café". The storefront is not already thriving and has no queue of purchasers. Back-left a slim four-storey office block; back-right a three-storey residential building with small balconies and a rooftop water tank; one modest low shop to the rear-left. Exactly four principal buildings, two short intersecting streets, white crossings, a few planters, two small benches, around seven carefully placed capsule/oval trees and a conifer. A few tiny blue/white cars, bicycles and naturally proportioned pedestrians, with a noticeable but restrained cluster of about a dozen people passing through one busy street. Keep the scene composed and airy, not a dense city map. It should be feasible to model and orbit in 3D.

Render exact copy on the left, with deliberate line breaks:
HEADLINE:
"A promising corner.
An important decision."
SUPPORT:
"Sid wanted to open a café.
This busy street caught his attention."

The 3D scene is the primary visual; text remains sharply readable. Establish the hopeful opportunity without suggesting that footfall proves demand. No demographic numbers, financial claims, fake statistics, colored analytical overlays yet, other scenes, comparison panels, border frames or watermarks.
assets.refinementPrompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Refine this exact 3D portfolio scene as the MASTER FRAME for a five-part story. Preserve its beautiful 3D architecture, blue-and-white materials, lighting, camera, arrangement, image dimensions, editorial layout and ALL copy exactly. Change ONLY the potential café premises in the foreground: it must be an unoccupied candidate storefront, since Sid has not opened his café yet. Remove the people sitting at café tables, all outdoor dining tables and chairs, the barista, prepared drinks, espresso counter and restaurant furniture visible inside this one storefront. Replace the interior with a quiet, clean unbranded vacant blue-white retail shell behind the glass, and its forecourt with a simple uncluttered sidewalk and the existing planters. Keep the blue-white awning, upper-story windows, rooftop HVAC, architectural shell and the "Potential café" label. Preserve all the other pedestrians walking past, all street life, other buildings, vehicles, trees and benches. The busy street should suggest opportunity while the prospective premises remain visibly unoccupied. Do not add a CLOSED sign, failure narrative, café name, other text or statistical data. Keep the same sophisticated 3D rendering, not a 2D drawing.
